introduction: This fourth Sunday of Easter is Good Shepherd Sunday, a day of prayer for vocations. Peter calls the crowd to repent and be baptized, and three thousand are added to the Church. Jesus says, I am the gate for the sheep; I came that they may have life, and have it abundantly. Peter tells us that we had gone astray like sheep but have returned to the shepherd of our souls. Let us listen to the shepherd's voice.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord is our shepherd; there is nothing we shall want. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For our Pope, our bishop and all the shepherds of the Church: that they may lead God's people with the heart of Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For vocations to the priesthood, the diaconate and religious life: that many may hear the voice of the Good Shepherd and follow. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who have gone astray: that they may return to the shepherd and guardian of their souls. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who suffer unjustly: that they may follow the example of Christ, who suffered for us. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may have life, and have it abundantly. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord Jesus, Good Shepherd, you call your sheep by name and lead them to life. Raise up shepherds for your Church, and keep us close to you. You live and reign for ever and ever.

reflection.title: Abundant life
reflection.body:
On the day of Pentecost, Peter tells the crowd that the Jesus they crucified is Lord and Christ. They are "cut to the heart" and ask, "Brothers, what shall we do?" Peter answers, "Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit." And he adds that the promise is "to you and to your children, and to all who are far off." That day, about three thousand people were baptized.

In the Gospel, Jesus uses the image of a sheepfold. The true shepherd enters by the gate, and "the sheep listen to his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out." The sheep follow him "for they know his voice." They will not follow a stranger.

Then Jesus says something surprising: "I am the door." He is not only the shepherd but the gate through which we enter into God's life. "If anyone enters in by me, he will be saved, and will go in and go out and will find pasture." And he tells us why he came: "I came that they may have life, and may have it abundantly." Jesus does not come to diminish our lives but to fill them.

Peter's letter shows the cost of this abundant life. Christ suffered for us, "leaving you an example, that you should follow his steps." "He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree... You were healed by his wounds." And he reminds us: "you were going astray like sheep; but now you have returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls."

Today we pray for vocations. Pray for the priests who have shepherded you. And this week, listen for Christ's voice among all the voices around you, and follow it.
